claims.text: Hip muscles: flexion (iliopsoas, rectus femoris), extension (gluteus maximus, hamstrings), abduction (gluteus medius and minimus), adduction (adductor longus, brevis and magnus).
claims.quote: Musc: flex (iliopsoas, rectus femoris), extend (gluteus maximus, hamstrings), abd (gluteus medius & minimus), add (adductor longus/brevis/magnus)

claims.text: Knee: the quadriceps extend and the hamstrings flex; supporting structures are the MCL/LCL, ACL/PCL, patellar and quadriceps tendons and the medial and lateral menisci.
claims.quote: Musc: quadriceps (knee extension), hamstrings (knee flexion) Connective tissue: MCL/LCL, ACL/PCL, patellar tendon, quad tendon, medial & lat menisci

claims.text: Menisci: distribute axial load and absorb shock.
claims.quote: medial & lat menisci: dist axial load + absorb shock

claims.text: Meniscus healing: the inner 2/3 of the meniscus is poorly vascular, so it heals poorly.
claims.quote: Avascular/poorly vasc (articular cartilage, inner annulus, inner 2/3 meniscus): slow diffusion from synovial fluid, ↓meta rate → heal poorly
claims.locator: Physiology & mechanics section, Vascular vs avascular healing

claims.text: Leg muscles: gastrocnemius and soleus plantarflex through the Achilles; tibialis anterior dorsiflexes; the fibularis (peroneal) muscles evert; tibialis posterior inverts.
claims.quote: Musc: gastrocnemius & soleus (plantarflexion via Achilles), tibialis anterior (dorsiflexion), fibularis/peroneal (eversion), tibialis posterior (inversion)

claims.text: Ankle ligaments: the lateral complex (ATFL, CFL, PTFL) and the medial deltoid ligament; also the Achilles tendon.
claims.quote: Connective tissue: lat complex (ATFL, CFL, PTFL), medial (deltoid), Achilles

claims.text: Knee joint cavity: the largest synovial cavity and a frequent site of effusion; posterior fluid forms a popliteal (Baker's) cyst.
claims.quote: Knee joint cavity = largest synovial cavity + frequent effusion site; posterior fluid → popliteal (Baker’s) cyst
claims.locator: Anatomy section, Synovial cavities, compartments & bursae

claims.text: Bursae: prepatellar (housemaid's knee), suprapatellar pouch, pes anserine, trochanteric (greater trochanteric pain syndrome), ischial and retrocalcaneal.
claims.quote: Bursae: prepatellar (“housemaid’s knee”), suprapatellar pouch, pes anserine, trochanteric (greater trochanteric pain syndrome), ischial, retrocalcaneal
claims.locator: Anatomy section, Synovial cavities, compartments & bursae

claims.text: Compartments: the leg has 4 fascial compartments (anterior, lateral, deep posterior, superficial posterior); the fascia does not stretch, which makes them the site of compartment syndrome.
claims.quote: Leg = 4 fascial compartments (A./lat/P deep/superficial P.); fascia ⍉stretch → compartment syndrome site
claims.locator: Anatomy section, Synovial cavities, compartments & bursae

claims.text: Nerves: sciatic (L4–S3) divides into the tibial and common fibular (peroneal) nerves; femoral (L2–L4) gives anterior thigh sensation and knee extension; obturator (L2–L4) gives adduction.
claims.quote: N.: sciatic (L4–S3) → tibial & common fibular (peroneal); femoral (L2–L4; A. thigh sensation + knee extend); obturator (L2–L4; add)

claims.text: Dermatomes: L4 runs medially to the big toe (knee jerk); L5 laterally to the dorsum and big toe (no reflex); S1 covers the posterior leg, lateral foot and sole (ankle jerk).
claims.quote: Dermatome: L4 = medial to big toe (knee-jerk); L5 = lat to dorsum/big toe (⍉reflex); S1 = P. leg, lat foot, sole (ankle-jerk)

claims.text: Pulses: femoral (femoral triangle), popliteal (popliteal fossa), dorsalis pedis, and posterior tibial (behind the medial malleolus).
claims.quote: Pulses: femoral (femoral triangle), popliteal (popliteal fossa), dorsalis pedis, P. tibial (post-medial malleolus)
